author: Thomas à Kempis
title: Of the love of solitude and silence

verses.text: Seek a suitable time for thy meditation, and think frequently of the mercies of God to thee.
verses.modernizedText: Seek a suitable time for meditation, and think frequently of God’s mercies to you.

verses.text: Leave curious questions.
verses.modernizedText: Leave curious questions aside.

verses.text: Study such matters as bring thee sorrow for sin rather than amusement.
verses.modernizedText: Study matters that bring you sorrow for sin rather than amusement.

verses.text: If thou withdraw thyself from trifling conversation and idle goings about, as well as from novelties and gossip, thou shalt find thy time sufficient and apt for good meditation.
verses.modernizedText: If you withdraw from trifling conversation and idle wandering, as well as from novelties and gossip, you will find your time sufficient and suitable for good meditation.

verses.text: The greatest saints used to avoid as far as they could the company of men, and chose to live in secret with God.
verses.modernizedText: The greatest saints used to avoid the company of others as far as they could and chose to live in secret with God.

verses.text: One hath said, “As oft as I have gone among men, so oft have I returned less a man.”
verses.modernizedText: Someone has said, “As often as I have gone among people, so often have I returned less a person.”

verses.text: This is what we often experience when we have been long time in conversation.
verses.modernizedText: This is what we often experience when we have spent a long time in conversation.

verses.text: For it is easier to be altogether silent than it is not to exceed in word.
verses.modernizedText: For it is easier to be altogether silent than not to speak too much.

verses.text: It is easier to remain hidden at home than to keep sufficient guard upon thyself out of doors.
verses.modernizedText: It is easier to remain hidden at home than to keep sufficient guard over yourself outside.

verses.text: He, therefore, that seeketh to reach that which is hidden and spiritual, must go with Jesus “apart from the multitude.”
verses.modernizedText: Therefore, anyone who seeks to reach what is hidden and spiritual must go with Jesus “apart from the multitude.”

verses.text: No man safely goeth abroad who loveth not to rest at home.
verses.modernizedText: No one goes abroad safely who does not love to rest at home.

verses.text: No man safely talketh but he who loveth to hold his peace.
verses.modernizedText: No one speaks safely except the person who loves to hold his peace.

verses.text: No man safely ruleth but he who loveth to be subject.
verses.modernizedText: No one rules safely except the person who loves to be subject.

verses.text: No man safely commandeth but he who loveth to obey.
verses.modernizedText: No one commands safely except the person who loves to obey.

verses.text: No man safely rejoiceth but he who hath the testimony of a good conscience within himself.
verses.modernizedText: No one rejoices safely except the person who has the testimony of a good conscience within himself.

verses.text: The boldness of the Saints was always full of the fear of God.
verses.modernizedText: The boldness of the Saints was always full of the fear of God.

verses.text: Nor were they the less earnest and humble in themselves, because they shone forth with great virtues and grace.
verses.modernizedText: Nor were they less earnest and humble in themselves because they shone with great virtues and grace.

verses.text: But the boldness of wicked men springeth from pride and presumption, and at the last turneth to their own confusion.
verses.modernizedText: But the boldness of the wicked springs from pride and presumption, and in the end turns to their own confusion.

verses.text: Never promise thyself security in this life, howsoever good a monk or devout a solitary thou seemest.
verses.modernizedText: Never promise yourself security in this life, however good a monk or devout a solitary you may seem.

verses.text: Often those who stand highest in the esteem of men, fall the more grievously because of their over great confidence.
verses.modernizedText: Often those who stand highest in the esteem of others fall more grievously because of their excessive confidence.

verses.text: Wherefore it is very profitable unto many that they should not be without inward temptation, but should be frequently assaulted, lest they be over confident, lest they be indeed lifted up into pride, or else lean too freely upon the consolations of the world.
verses.modernizedText: Therefore, it is very profitable for many not to be without inward temptation, but to be frequently assaulted, lest they become overconfident, be lifted up in pride, or lean too freely on the consolations of the world.

verses.text: O how good a conscience should that man keep, who never sought a joy that passeth away, who never became entangled with the world!
verses.modernizedText: Oh, what a good conscience the person would keep who never sought a passing joy and never became entangled with the world!

verses.text: O how great peace and quiet should he possess, who would cast off all vain care, and think only of healthful and divine things, and build his whole hope upon God!
verses.modernizedText: Oh, what great peace and quiet he would possess who cast off all vain care, thought only of healthful and divine things, and built his whole hope on God!

verses.text: No man is worthy of heavenly consolation but he who hath diligently exercised himself in holy compunction.
verses.modernizedText: No one is worthy of heavenly consolation except the person who has diligently exercised himself in holy compunction.

verses.text: If thou wilt feel compunction within thy heart, enter into thy chamber and shut out the tumults of the world, as it is written, Commune with your own heart in your own chamber and be still.(1) In retirement thou shalt find what often thou wilt lose abroad.
verses.modernizedText: If you want to feel compunction in your heart, enter your chamber and shut out the tumults of the world, as it is written, Commune with your own heart in your own chamber and be still.(1) In solitude you will find what you will often lose abroad.

verses.text: Retirement, if thou continue therein, groweth sweet, but if thou keep not in it, begetteth weariness.
verses.modernizedText: Solitude, if you continue in it, grows sweet, but if you do not keep to it, it produces weariness.

verses.text: If in the beginning of thy conversation thou dwell in it and keep it well, it shall afterwards be to thee a dear friend, and a most pleasant solace.
verses.modernizedText: If at the beginning of your conversion you dwell in it and keep it well, it will afterward be a dear friend and a most pleasant solace to you.

verses.text: In silence and quiet the devout soul goeth forward and learneth the hidden things of the Scriptures.
verses.modernizedText: In silence and quiet the devout soul goes forward and learns the hidden things of the Scriptures.

verses.text: Therein findeth she a fountain of tears, wherein to wash and cleanse herself each night, that she may grow the more dear to her Maker as she dwelleth the further from all worldly distraction.
verses.modernizedText: There she finds a fountain of tears in which to wash and cleanse herself each night, so that she may grow dearer to her Maker as she dwells farther from all worldly distraction.

verses.text: To him who withdraweth himself from his acquaintance and friends God with his holy angels will draw nigh.
verses.modernizedText: God with His holy angels will draw near to the person who withdraws from his acquaintances and friends.

verses.text: It is better to be unknown and take heed to oneself than to neglect oneself and work wonders.
verses.modernizedText: It is better to be unknown and take heed to oneself than to neglect oneself and work wonders.

verses.text: It is praiseworthy for a religious man to go seldom abroad, to fly from being seen, to have no desire to see men.
verses.modernizedText: It is praiseworthy for a religious person to go out seldom, to flee from being seen, and to have no desire to see others.

verses.text: Why wouldest thou see what thou mayest not have?
verses.modernizedText: Why would you see what you may not have?

verses.text: The world passeth away and the lust thereof.
verses.modernizedText: The world passes away and its lust.

verses.text: The desires of sensuality draw thee abroad, but when an hour is past, what dost thou bring home, but a weight upon thy conscience and distraction of heart?
verses.modernizedText: The desires of sensuality draw you out, but when an hour has passed, what do you bring home except a weight on your conscience and distraction of heart?

verses.text: A merry going forth bringeth often a sorrowful return, and a merry evening maketh a sad morning?
verses.modernizedText: A merry departure often brings a sorrowful return, and a merry evening makes a sad morning?

verses.text: So doth all carnal joy begin pleasantly, but in the end it gnaweth away and destroyeth.
verses.modernizedText: So all carnal joy begins pleasantly, but in the end it gnaws away and destroys.

verses.text: What canst thou see abroad which thou seest not at home?
verses.modernizedText: What can you see abroad that you do not see at home?

verses.text: Behold the heaven and the earth and the elements, for out of these are all things made.
verses.modernizedText: Behold the heaven and the earth and the elements, for out of these all things are made.

verses.text: What canst thou see anywhere which can continue long under the sun?
verses.modernizedText: What can you see anywhere that can continue long under the sun?

verses.text: Thou believest perchance that thou shalt be satisfied, but thou wilt never be able to attain unto this.
verses.modernizedText: Perhaps you believe that you will be satisfied, but you will never be able to attain this.

verses.text: If thou shouldest see all things before thee at once, what would it be but a vain vision?
verses.modernizedText: If you saw all things before you at once, what would it be but a vain vision?

verses.text: Lift up thine eyes to God on high, and pray that thy sins and negligences may be forgiven.
verses.modernizedText: Lift up your eyes to God on high, and pray that your sins and neglect may be forgiven.

verses.text: Leave vain things to vain men, and mind thou the things which God hath commanded thee.
verses.modernizedText: Leave vain things to vain people, and attend to the things God has commanded you.

verses.text: Shut thy door upon thee, and call unto thyself Jesus thy beloved.
verses.modernizedText: Shut your door upon yourself and call Jesus your beloved to yourself.

verses.text: Remain with Him in thy chamber, for thou shalt not elsewhere find so great peace.
verses.modernizedText: Remain with Him in your chamber, for you will not find such great peace elsewhere.

verses.text: If thou hadst not gone forth nor listened to vain talk, thou hadst better kept thyself in good peace.
verses.modernizedText: If you had not gone out or listened to vain talk, you would have kept yourself in better peace.

verses.text: But because it sometimes delighteth thee to hear new things, thou must therefore suffer trouble of heart.
verses.modernizedText: But because you sometimes delight to hear new things, you must therefore suffer trouble of heart.
